lq.ANSWER:
1. Problem & Paradigm Used (4 marks)

  • Problem: Analyzing and filtering large user log files.

  • Paradigm: Functional programming used for cleaner, modular data processing.

2. Implementation (7 marks)

Using map(), filter(), and lambda:

logs = ["error: disk", "info: start", "error: memory"] error_logs = list(filter(lambda x: x.startswith("error"), logs)) print(error_logs) # ['error: disk', 'error: memory']

  • Code avoids side effects and uses pure functions for clarity and reuse.

3. Evaluation (4 marks)

  • Functional paradigm improved code readability and testability.

  • Encouraged modular design, making debugging and updates easier.

  • Helped avoid bugs caused by shared mutable state.
lq.QUESTION_DESC:
You are asked to develop a mini project in Python that incorporates at least one programming paradigm (functional, logic, or parallel/distributed computing). The goal is to solve a real-world problem such as processing user data, analyzing logs, or automating a task.

Task:

  1. Describe the real-world problem your project addresses and identify the programming paradigm used. (4 marks)

  2. Explain with code how key concepts of the chosen paradigm are implemented (e.g., pure functions, Prolog rules, multiprocessing). (7 marks)

  3. Evaluate the advantages of using this paradigm in your project and how it influenced the design and outcome. (4 marks)
